question: In the bubbling fluidized bed, why did the measured NO emissions fall as the NH3 co-firing ratio rose from 0 to 20% at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0?
rendered: The measured NO emissions fell as the NH3 co-firing ratio rose from 0 to 20% at a PA/SA ratio of 1:0 because as the proportion of primary air (PA) decreased, the amount of excess oxygen required for combustion was reduced, leading to more NH3 being consumed by reduction reactions rather than by NO formation at the low temperature of 1100 K.
